source_text: Ὁ γὰρ τὴν φυλακὴν τῶν μαρτύρων πεπιστευμένος, ἐγγύθεν ἀπό τινος γυμνασίου διαθαλπόμενος, ἀπεσκόπει τὸ μέλλον, ἕτοιμος προσδέχεσθαι τῶν στρατιωτῶν τοὺς προσ φεύγοντας. Καὶ γὰρ αὖ καὶ τοῦτο, ἐγγύθεν εἶναι λουτρὸν, ἐπενοήθη, ὀξεῖαν τὴν βοήθειαν τοῖς μετα βαλλομένοις ἐπαγγελλόμενον. Ὅπερ μέντοι τοῖς ἐναντίοις κακούργως ἐπενοήθη, τοιοῦτον ἐξευρεῖν τῆς ἀθλήσεως τόπον, ἐν ᾧ τὸ ἕτοιμον τῆς παραμυθίας ἐκλύειν ἔμελλε τῶν ἀγωνιζομένων τὴν ἔνστασιν· τοῦτο λαμπροτέραν ἐδείκνυε τὴν ὑπομονὴν τῶν μαρτύρων. Οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀπορῶν τῶν ἀναγκαίων καρτερικὸς, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐν ἀφθονίᾳ τῆς ἀπολαύσεως ἐγκαρτερῶν τοῖς δεινοῖς. Ὡς δὲ οἱ μὲν ἠγωνίζοντο, ὁ δὲ ἐπετήρει τὸ ἐκβησόμενον, εἶδε θέαμα ξένον, δυνάμεις τινὰς ἐξ οὐρανῶν κατιούσας, καὶ οἷον παρὰ βασιλέως δωρεὰς μεγάλας διανεμούσας τοῖς στρατιώταις· αἳ τοῖς μὲν ἄλλοις πᾶσι διῄρουν τὰ δῶρα, ἕνα δὲ μόνον ἀφῆκαν ἀγέραστον, ἀνάξιον κρίνασαι τῶν οὐρανίων τιμῶν· ὃς εὐθὺς, πρὸς τοὺς πόνους ἀπαγορεύσας, πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἀπηυτομόλησεν. Ἐλεεινὸν θέαμα τοῖς δικαίοις ὁ στρατιώτης φυγὰς, ὁ ἀριστεὺς αἰχμάλωτος, τὸ Χριστοῦ πρόβατον θηριάλωτον· καὶ τό γε ἐλεεινότερον, ὅτι καὶ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς διήμαρτε, καὶ οὐδὲ ταύτης ἀπήλαυσεν, εὐθὺς αὐτῷ τῆς σαρκὸς ἐν τῇ προσβολῇ τῆς θέρμης διαλυθείσης. Καὶ ὁ μὲν φιλόζωος ἔπεσεν ἀνομήσας διακενῆς· ὁ δὲ δήμιος, ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἐκκλίναντα, καὶ πρὸς τὸ βαλανεῖον ἀποδραμόντα, ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ λειποτακτήσαντος χώραν ἀντικατέστησε, καὶ ῥίψας τὰ περιβόλαια, τοῖς γυμνοῖς ἑαυτὸν ἐγκατέμιξε, κράζων τὴν αὐτὴν βοὴν τοῖς ἁγίοις· Χριστιανός εἰμι. Καὶ τῷ ἀθρόῳ τῆς μεταβολῆς ἐκπλήξας τοὺς συμπαρόντας, τόν τε ἀριθμὸν ἀνεπλήρωσε, καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τῷ καταμαλακι σθέντι λύπην τῇ παρ' ἑαυτοῦ προσθήκῃ παρεμυθήσατο, μιμησάμενος τοὺς ἐπὶ παρατάξεως, οἳ, τοῦ κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἀσπίδα πεσόντος, εὐθὺς ἀναπληροῦσι τὴν φάλαγγα, ὡς μὴ τὸν συνασπισμὸν αὐτοῖς διακοπῆναι τῷ λείποντι. Τοιοῦτον δή τι καὶ αὐτὸς ἐποίησεν. Εἶδε τὰ οὐράνια θαύματα, ἐπέγνω τὴν ἀλήθειαν, προσέφυγε τῷ Δεσπότῃ, συνηριθμήθη τοῖς μάρτυσι. Τὰ τῶν μαθητῶν ἀνενεώσατο. Ἀπῆλθεν Ἰούδας, καὶ ἀντεισήχθη Ματθίας. Μιμητὴς ἐγένετο Παύλου, ὁ χθὲς διώκτης, σήμερον εὐαγγελιζόμενος. Ἄνωθεν ἔσχε καὶ αὐτὸς τὴν κλῆσιν, Οὐκ ἀπ' ἀν θρώπων, οὐδὲ δι' ἀνθρώπου. Ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς αὐτὸν, οὐχ ὑπὸ ἄλλου, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ τῆς οἰκείας πί στεως· οὐκ ἐν ὕδατι, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ αἵματι. Καὶ οὕτως, ἡμέρας ἀρχομένης, ἔτι ἐμπνέοντες τῷ πυρὶ παρεδόθησαν, καὶ τὰ τοῦ πυρὸς λείψανα ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν ἀπεῤῥίφη· ὥστε διὰ πάσης τῆς κτίσεως διεξελθεῖν τῶν μακαρίων τὴν ἄθλησιν. Ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἠγωνίσαντο, τῷ ἀέρι ἐνεκαρτέρησαν, τῷ πυρὶ παρεδόθησαν, τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοὺς ὑπεδέξατο. Ἐκείνων ἐστὶν ἡ φωνή· Διήλθομεν διὰ πυρὸς καὶ ὕδατος, καὶ ἐξήγαγες ἡμᾶς εἰς ἀναψυχήν. Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὴν καθ' ἡμᾶς χώραν διαλαβόντες, οἱονεὶ πύργοι τινὲς συνεχεῖς, ἀσφάλειαν ἐκ τῆς τῶν ἐναν τίων καταδρομῆς παρεχόμενοι, οὐχ ἑνὶ τόπῳ ἑαυ τοὺς κατακλείσαντες, ἀλλὰ πολλοῖς ἤδη ἐπιξενωθέντες χωρίοις, καὶ πολλὰς πατρίδας κατακοσμή σαντες. Καὶ τὸ παράδοξον, οὐ καθ' ἕνα διαμερισθέντες τοῖς δεχομένοις ἐπιφοιτῶσιν· ἀλλ' ἀναμιχθέντες ἀλλήλοις, ἡνωμένως χορεύουσιν.
thought_title: The guard takes the deserter's place
orientation: Basil is narrating the climax of the Forty's contest: the guard watching the freezing martyrs sees heavenly powers distributing crowns, and when one soldier deserts, the guard confesses Christ and joins the martyrs in his place.
pass_a_gloss: For the one entrusted with the guard of the martyrs, being warmed from nearby from some warm room, was watching what was going to happen, ready to receive the soldiers who were fleeing over. For indeed this too, that a bath was nearby, had been devised, promising swift help to those changing sides. What indeed was wickedly devised by the enemies, to find such a place for the contest, in which the readiness of comfort was going to dissolve the steadfastness of the contestants; this showed more brightly the endurance of the martyrs. For not the one lacking necessities is steadfast, but the one in abundance of enjoyment enduring in terrible things. And as they were contending, and he was watching what would come out, he saw a strange sight, certain powers coming down from heaven, and as it were from a king distributing great gifts to the soldiers; and they divided the gifts among all the others, but one alone they left without a gift, judging him unworthy of the heavenly honors; who immediately, having given up on the toils, deserted to the enemies. A pitiable sight to the righteous was the soldier a fugitive, the champion a captive, the sheep of Christ caught by wild beasts; and the more pitiable thing, that he both missed eternal life, and did not enjoy even this present life, his flesh immediately dissolving in the assault of the heat. And the life-lover fell, having broken faith in vain; but the executioner, when he saw him turning aside and running off to the bath, placed himself in the deserter's place, and throwing off his garments, mixed himself with the naked ones, crying the same cry as the saints: I am a Christian. And by the suddenness of the change amazing those present, he both filled up the number, and comforted the grief over the one who had grown soft by his own addition, imitating those in battle line, who, when the one in the first shield has fallen, immediately fill up the phalanx, so that the shield-wall may not be broken for them by the missing one. Such a thing indeed he himself also did. He saw the heavenly wonders, he recognized the truth, he fled for refuge to the Master, he was numbered with the martyrs. He renewed the things of the disciples. Judas departed, and Matthias was brought in. He became an imitator of Paul, the one yesterday a persecutor, today preaching the gospel. From above he also had the calling, not from men, nor through a man. He believed in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; he was baptized into him, not by another, but by his own faith; not in water, but in his own blood. And thus, as day was beginning, still breathing they were handed over to the fire, and the remains of the fire were cast into the river; so that through all creation the contest of the blessed ones passed. On the earth they contended, in the air they endured, to the fire they were handed over, the water received them. Theirs is the voice: We went through fire and water, and you brought us out into refreshment. These are the ones who have taken hold of our region, like certain continuous towers, providing security from the onslaught of enemies, not shutting themselves up in one place, but already having been received as guests in many places, and having adorned many homelands. And the paradox: not divided one by one do they visit those who receive them; but mixed with one another, unitedly they dance in company.

choices.why: The context is the guard warming himself near the bath; γυμνάσιον here denotes a heated room or bathhouse, not an exercise ground.
ἀνομήσας here means transgressing against God's law by deserting the contest, not general lawlessness.
χώραν means the deserter's position or spot among the martyrs, not military ranks.

choices.english: the one yesterday a persecutor, today preaching the gospel
choices.why: The participles with the article mark him as 'the one who'—anaphoric force pointing to the guard as a new Paul.
rejected: yesterday a persecutor, today preaching the gospel

choices.english: mixed with one another, unitedly they dance in company
choices.why: χορεύουσιν is rendered 'dance in company' to preserve the corporate, united movement of the martyrs as a single company.

pass_b_english: The man entrusted with guarding the martyrs was warming himself nearby at some gymnasium, watching for what would happen, ready to receive any of the soldiers who fled over to him. For this too had been devised: that a bath was nearby, promising swift relief to those who changed their minds. What the enemy had maliciously contrived—finding a place for the contest where the ready comfort would weaken the steadfastness of the contestants—this very thing made the endurance of the martyrs shine more brightly. For it is not the one who lacks necessities who shows endurance, but the one who holds fast amid an abundance of enjoyment. As they were contending and he was watching for the outcome, he saw a strange sight: powers descending from heaven, distributing great gifts to the soldiers as if from a king. To all the others they divided the gifts, but one alone they left without a gift, judging him unworthy of heavenly honors—who, immediately giving up on the struggle, deserted to the enemy. A pitiful sight to the righteous: the soldier a fugitive, the champion a captive, Christ's sheep caught by wild beasts. And what was more pitiful still: he both missed eternal life and did not enjoy this present life, for his flesh dissolved at once when the heat struck him. The lover of life fell, having broken faith to no purpose. But the guard, when he saw him turn aside and run to the bath, put himself in the deserter's place, threw off his garments, and joined himself to the naked ones, crying out the same cry as the saints: "I am a Christian." By the suddenness of his change he astonished those present, filled up the number, and comforted the grief over the one who had weakened by his own addition—imitating those in battle line who, when the man in the first shield falls, immediately fill the gap in the phalanx so that their shield-wall is not broken by the missing one. Something like this he did. He saw the heavenly wonders, recognized the truth, fled for refuge to the Master, and was numbered with the martyrs. He restored the company of the disciples: Judas departed, and Matthias was brought in. He became an imitator of Paul—the one yesterday a persecutor, today preaching the gospel. He too had his call from above, not from men nor through a man. He believed in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; he was baptized into Him, not by another but by his own faith, not in water but in his own blood. And so, as day was beginning, still breathing they were handed over to the fire, and the remains of the fire were cast into the river, so that the contest of the blessed ones passed through all creation. On earth they contended, in the air they endured, to fire they were handed over, the water received them. Theirs is the voice: "We went through fire and water, and You brought us out to refreshment" (Psalm 65:12 (Hebrew 66:12)). These are the ones who have taken hold of our region, like continuous towers providing security against the assaults of the enemy—not shutting themselves up in one place, but already visiting many districts and adorning many homelands. And the wonder is that they do not come to those who receive them divided one by one, but mixed with one another, unitedly they move in company.

problems.why: χορεύουσιν here means 'move in chorus/company' (metaphorical united movement), not literal dancing; 'company' alone from glossary is better.
γυμνασίου means exercise ground/stadium, not a room; the guard warms himself near a gymnasium.
problems.fix: warming himself nearby at some exercise ground
problems.ruling: γυμνασίου means gymnasium/exercise ground, not 'warm room'; mistranslation changes the setting.

problems.why: This is Psalm 65:12 in LXX numbering (Psalm 66:12 is Hebrew numbering); brief requires Septuagint numbering.
